questions.title: Day of the Week Decoder with Default Case
questions.question: Write a Java program that takes an integer from 1 to 7 and uses a traditional switch statement with a default case to map the number to its corresponding day name[cite: 16].
questions.explanation: A traditional switch statement in Java evaluates an expression against multiple constant case labels[cite: 16]. Compatible selector expressions include byte, short, char, int, their respective wrapper types, enums, and String[cite: 5, 16]. In this implementation, the integer selector is evaluated sequentially against integer case literals 1 through 7[cite: 16]. Each case block must conclude with a break statement; omitting break triggers fall-through, causing execution to spill into subsequent case blocks regardless of whether their condition matches[cite: 16]. The default label acts as a catch-all branch that executes when none of the defined case values match the selector, ensuring reliable boundary handling for out-of-range inputs[cite: 16].
hints: Include an explicit `break;` statement at the conclusion of every case block to prevent unwanted fall-through[cite: 16].
Place a `default:` label at the end of the switch block to handle invalid numbers outside the 1–7 range[cite: 16].
Print both the input selector number and the mapped day string[cite: 16].

questions.title: Vowel Classifier via Stacked Fall-Through Cases

questions.explanation: In traditional Java switch statements, omitting a break statement between cases causes control to fall through sequentially to the next statement[cite: 16]. While unintended fall-through is a frequent source of bugs, intentional fall-through allows multiple distinct case values to share an identical execution path[cite: 16]. By stacking `case 'a': case 'e': case 'i': case 'o': case 'u':` contiguously without intermediate statements or breaks, any vowel character flows down to the single assignment statement before terminating at the break[cite: 16]. A default label catches all remaining characters, categorizing them as consonants or non-vowels[cite: 16].

questions.title: Calendar Days per Month Calculator with Leap Year Logic

February (month 2) forms its own isolated branch where leap year rules must be evaluated: if `(year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)`, February has 29 days; otherwise, it has 28[cite: 7, 13, 16]. Any month outside 1-12 falls to default and returns -1[cite: 16].
